tasks.task: Build a welcome flow for new subscribers

items.when: When a shop has an offer, best sellers and a story and needs the flow's timing, filters and outlines
When each welcome email is drafted, to compare subject lines in several angles
When few people join the list, to fix the popup that feeds the flow
Before the flow is built, to plan three different arcs for new subscribers and draft each first email
Before the flow goes live, to score each email and get a ship or fix verdict

tasks.task: Build abandoned cart and browse flows

items.when: When the shop has no flows yet and needs a safe order to switch them on
When you know margin and shipping terms and need cart and checkout recovery emails with timing
When shoppers view products and leave, to get a browse flow that holds any discount to the end
When the first cart email is drafted, to try several openings against each other
When a flow has numbers, to mark what to protect and what to fix

tasks.task: Build a reorder flow timed to how long the product lasts

items.when: Before building, to set the reminder day from real order gaps, not one fixed day
When you know how long each product lasts and need reorder and refill messages
When buyers differ by type and you want timed emails per type, then a read of results
Before the reminders go live, to score each one and fix the weak one

tasks.task: Plan how first orders become repeat buyers

items.when: Before any fix, to find the one stage where first-time buyers stop
When delivery times are known and you need the thank-you, how-to, add-on and review emails
When the second-order email needs a product to suggest, from what buyers pair together
When the parcel itself should earn the next order, with a costed insert and gift rule
When the flow should ask for a review at the right moment and in the right words

tasks.task: Win back lapsed buyers without a big discount

items.when: When a pile of one-time buyers must come back without training everyone to wait for a code
When you know the usual gap between orders and need a flow timed to it
When win-back and list cleaning should run together, with a read of results
When you need to know which repeat buyers are overdue before you write to anyone
When the hook should be a gift, bundle or early access, not money off
Before writing the win-back emails, to compare three approaches that do not lean on a discount
Before the win-back run starts, to score each email and cut what drags

tasks.task: Plan a month of campaign emails that sell without discounts

items.when: When the shop needs a topic bank, a month calendar and written emails in one run
When one campaign needs writing block by block from product facts
When a campaign is written, to pick from subject lines in several angles
When a designer will build the email and needs a section-by-section brief
Before each send, to get cuts, a score and a ship or fix verdict
When the emails talk about the shop and should start from what the reader wants

tasks.task: Plan a sale across email and SMS

items.when: Before a sale weekend or launch, to set who gets what, how often and what the offer costs
When the plan is agreed and you need the send calendar, emails and checked texts
When the sale needs engaged, buyer and exclusion groups defined with clear rules
Before the offer is set, to find the deepest discount the margin allows

tasks.task: Launch or restart the SMS channel

items.when: When a shop starts texting, moves platform or restarts after opt-outs and complaints
When consent wording, quiet hours and send frequency must be set or checked
Before the first send, to see who agreed to texts and who did not
When the channel is live and needs a month of texts and a frequency test

tasks.task: Write and check a pack of marketing texts

items.when: When you need texts for welcome, cart, win-back or a promo with consent rules built in
Just before a batch or new text flow goes live, to catch consent, timing and wording faults
When one text is ready, to check its cost, length and rule flags

tasks.task: Design a subscription offer the shop can afford

items.when: When a shop wants a subscription and needs the offer, the perks and an honest way out
When you have price, margin and cash and need the offer and the most to pay per subscriber
When the launch needs the offer, its payback time and the cancel flow in one run
Before launch, to test whether the offer pays back in time for the cash on hand
When the offer is live, to score how well the product page sells the subscription
When subscribers need clear billing reminders and order confirmations before each charge

tasks.task: Audit where buyers and subscribers stop

items.when: When you have an order or subscriber export and need to see where customers stop buying
Before reading an export, to catch blanks, duplicates and stale rows that would skew it
When you need repeat rate and revenue for each first-purchase month
When the business is subscription, to score where subscribers leave
When the owner asks if repeat orders pay back the cost of winning a customer

tasks.task: Build an honest cancel, pause and skip path

items.when: When the cancel route must be easy to find and offer pause or skip without tricks
When you know the cancel reasons and portal options and need one save per reason
When you want a second design with save offers and failed-payment recovery to compare

tasks.task: Read cancel reasons and choose one fix

items.when: Once a month, to turn cancel reasons into one fair save per reason and one product fix
When you must match saves to what the subscription tool can really do
When nobody collects reasons yet and you need the survey questions first
Each month, to see if last month's fix worked and where subscribers leave now

tasks.task: Run the monthly retention fix

items.when: In the first week of each month, for a shop with a few months of order history
When the monthly run should find the weakest repeat stage and fix it
When the weakest flow should be found and rebuilt each month with its copy checked
When last month's numbers are in, to see what broke and what to repeat

tasks.task: Design a loyalty, VIP or referral programme

items.when: When you have spend tiers and margins and want perks that are not discounts
When the best customers should get a named programme and personal touches
When a refer-a-friend reward may do more than points and you want it planned
Before launch, to test the programme's sums against its cost and who it reaches
When the plan only rewards heavy buyers and ignores the many who buy once a year

tasks.task: Segment the list by value, recency and stage

items.when: When you need every customer scored on recency, frequency and spend and put in a group
When the groups must become send and exclusion rules in the email tool
When one flow treats new, returning and loyal buyers the same and needs splitting

tasks.task: Fix deliverability and clean the list

items.when: When opens fall, to score the sending set-up and DNS records and list the fixes
When SPF, DKIM or DMARC are missing or wrong on the sending domain
When emails land in spam and you have 60 days of results to work from
When the list holds people who never open, to set a sunset flow and a monthly clean

tasks.task: Audit the existing flows and find what is missing

items.when: When you inherit an account, to find missing steps and rules that clash
When one flow has numbers, to sort it into protect, watch and fix
When the audit names the weakest flow and it needs a rebuild

tasks.task: Measure what retention work really adds

items.when: When the platform's revenue figure is doubted, to design a holdout and how to read it
When there are many ideas to test, to rank them with sample sizes and win rules
When a test has ended, to see if the difference is real before acting on it
When you want orders by campaign from the shop's own order lines, not the email tool
When flows take credit for sales that would have happened anyway

tasks.task: Grow the list with a popup or quiz

items.when: When you need desktop and mobile popup specs, copy and tests for the offer
When a quiz may beat a discount popup and should sort people into the right flow
When two popup versions run, to set the sample size and the rule for a winner

tasks.task: Turn approved copy into an email layout or HTML

items.when: When a designer builds the email and needs each section briefed
When you want two HTML designs with previews to choose between
When the shop sends from Klaviyo and you need to know what its flows and blocks can do
Before the built email is scheduled, to score it and catch what to cut

always.when: Before any email or text goes out, to fix off-voice words without touching claims
When copy states a number, a result or a guarantee you cannot trace to the shop

helpers.when: When the job is newsletters, platform set-up or a deliverability problem that needs deep work
When repeat rate, lifetime value or cohorts must be modelled from raw order data
When a subscription app, checkout change or customer tag must be set up in the store
When a flow needs long-form selling copy or a landing page behind it
When cancel reasons are thin and customers must be interviewed about why they left
When the subscription price, discount depth or tiers need a proper pricing study

gaps: No library item writes a failed payment recovery run on its own; it sits inside two churn items
No library item checks a cancel path against click-to-cancel and auto-renewal rules by region
No library item builds a back-in-stock, price-drop or birthday flow
No library item designs a preference centre or an unsubscribe page with frequency choices
No library item covers SMS consent set-up by region, sender registration and quiet hours; only the kit does
No library item writes several clearly different versions of one text or flow email to test side by side
No library item plans a move between email platforms: flows, suppression lists and warm-up
No library item reads a flow's true added revenue from a platform export with a holdout group
No library item covers push or in-app messages for shops with an app
